Getting started

Quick start

Create a disposable Flutter app, initialize Kite, generate two architecture styles, and verify the complete output.

Create a Flutter project

Use a separate project for your first test so you can inspect every generated file safely.

Preview project initialization

Use --dry-run to see the generation plan before writing anything.

Generate foundations and features

Add Clean Architecture, MVC, reusable components, Riverpod, and Dio as needed.

Analyze the result

Install dependencies, format source, run analysis, and launch the app.

Complete smoke test

cd ~/Desktop
flutter create kite_test_app
cd kite_test_app

kite init --dry-run
kite init

kite --feat:clean dashboard --route
kite --feat:mvc profile --route
kite --widget "[button,card,avatar]"
kite --state riverpod
kite --api:dio

flutter pub get
dart format .
flutter analyze
flutter test
flutter run

What you should see

lib/ ├── app/ │ ├── router/ │ └── theme/ ├── core/ │ ├── errors/ │ ├── network/ │ ├── result/ │ └── state/ ├── features/ │ ├── dashboard/ │ └── profile/ ├── shared/ │ ├── components/ │ └── widgets/ └── main.dart

Use canonical commands when scripting

Shorthand is convenient at the terminal. Canonical subcommands are clearer in team documentation and automation:

kite feature dashboard --architecture clean --route
kite feature profile --architecture mvc --route
kite component button card avatar
kite state riverpod
kite api dio
!
JSON generation requires one extra command

After adding real fields to a model or DTO generated with --json, run dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs.
